newsitem.title: USA: Bankruptcies up, but economy is well - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Bankruptcies up, but economy is well - Greenspan.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Saturday the economy was doing well despite a sharp rise in personal bankruptcies.

"We don't know why personal bankruptcies have soared as sharply as they have, especially considering the fact that the economy is doing so well and consumers in general are doing well," Greenspan said after a speech at the Conference of State Bank Supervisors.

"I'm not concerned that it will create any issues beyond the immediate credit card problem, but there is no question that this issue is a considerable amount of concern to banks," he said during the question and answer period.

Greenspan said he believed that actions currently under way at banks will be more than adequate to resolve the problem, citing considerably more awareness about lending risks and a pullback in issuance of new cards.
Greenspan said that personal bankruptcies have evolved faster than in the past.
"Models suggested that after a period of time you would expect a bankruptcy would evolve," he said.
"But instead of dealing with 30 and 60 day delinquencies that would eventually lead to bankruptcy, what we find is that they go from fairly serious immediately into bankruptcy."
The Fed chief spoke to the group by teleconference.
In his speech, Greenspan said financial system reform should not reduce the Federal Reserve's bank supervisory authority because the Fed needs to guard against market disruption.
